messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Entropy change for a 1 kg ice block heated from 0 °C to 100 °C at 1 atm**

| Process | Temperature (K) | Heat exchanged (J kg⁻¹) | Entropy change (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Melting (0 °C → 0 °C) | 273.15 | \(L_f = 334\,000\) | \(\displaystyle \frac{L_f}{T_m}= \frac{334\,000}{273.15}\approx 1\,222\) |
| Heating liquid water (0 °C → 100 °C) | 273.15 → 373.15 | \(c_{\text{water}}\Delta T = 4\,186\times(373.15-273.15)=418\,600\) | \(\displaystyle c_{\text{water}}\ln\frac{T_f}{T_i}=4\,186\ln\frac{373.15}{273.15}\approx 1\,307\) |
| Vaporising (100 °C → 100 °C) | 373.15 | \(L_v = 2\,260\,000\) | \(\displaystyle \frac{L_v}{T_b}= \frac{2\,260\,000}{373.15}\approx 6\,055\) |
| **Total** | – | – | **≈ 8 584 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹** |

So the entropy of the system increases by **≈ 8.6 kJ K⁻¹** when a 1‑kg ice block at 0 °C is heated to 100 °C under 1 atm.
